title: Tests have three tiers, and the production smoke test is a subset of end-to-end
context: ADR-0085 defined a fourth tier, the API smoke test, that called a deployed backend with no client, and made both it and end-to-end tests wait on a test-only sign-in path. Planning the production smoke test showed that an HTTP-only check cannot see the cookie behaviour that differs between WebKit and Chromium, which is where sign-in on the iOS app most often fails, and that the production smoke test needs no test-only sign-in path: it signs in for real once and reuses that session.
decision: A unit test runs in one process and does no I/O, however many real collaborators it uses. An integration test reaches at least one real out-of-process dependency, and proving behaviour that needs it is its purpose. An end-to-end test drives a real client, the web app in a browser or a mobile app, against a deployed backend: one suite per client, covering critical paths only. A test's tier follows from what it touches, not from its folder or its entry point. There is no separate API smoke tier: a check against a deployed backend is an end-to-end test, even when it makes HTTP requests without opening a page. The production smoke test is the subset of end-to-end tests tagged @smoke that runs against production after promotion, signed in with a real session established once by a person; it never uses a test-only sign-in path. Only end-to-end tests outside production use a test-only sign-in path, and that path must never reach production.

alternatives.option: Keep API smoke as a fourth tier for the production checks
alternatives.reason: An HTTP-only check cannot observe browser cookie handling, so it would miss the WebKit sign-in failures the production smoke test exists to catch, and a fourth directory breaks the three-tier layout of unit beside the code and integration and end-to-end under test/.

alternatives.option: Give the production smoke test its own directory, such as test/smoke/
alternatives.reason: Smoke describes a purpose, not what a test touches; a tag selects the subset without creating a tier that the file-name check would have to know about.

consequences: End-to-end tests live in test/e2e/ as *.e2e.ts; the production smoke test is selected with --grep @smoke.

The production smoke test can be built without a test-only sign-in path; end-to-end tests outside production still wait on one, and on the environments no longer sharing a database and auth secret with production.
revisitTriggers: A mobile client is built: its end-to-end suite needs its own selection of the production smoke test.
Spec-driven acceptance tests are adopted: they are classified by this same rule, which may call for a directory of their own.
